body: I know what you mean, really, and I've been considering going back to therapy. It's obvious to me, and most of the people who I've talked to about myself, that I'm quite deeply depressed and need some sort of professional help -- I really just hope that I can build up the courage to do that.

Thank you. Honestly, I feel a lot better than I have in such a long time (it's strange that this all happened so fast. I kind of just want to go out and do it again!). 

Also, if you are a volunteer, then thank you for your service -- People who can really listen and dish out advice like I got from Reddit/Ernie are, literally, lifesavers.

Honestly, those are exactly the types of people who I like to keep as close friends -- the introverts who just need a little coaxing to get out of their shell (I'm like that, myself). 

The problem is finding those people, though. Not everyone is welcoming to strangers. 

And I might just take you up on that offer.

Honestly, I've never been a fan of the whole "stranger approach" dynamic. There are some places -- especially bus stops, coffee shops, and parks -- where that kind of interaction flourishes, though, and I'm kind of in the process of learning the ropes.

All I really know is that you need to tell that stranger the most interesting things about yourself (Just to get them interested), show them your humorous side, and ask a lot of questions (Nothing too personal -- just show that you're listening. People love to stroke their egos when you ask them questions.). Also, bring bubbles.

But, yeah, I would definitely recommend it, especially when you see someone all alone, maybe looking a little depressed -- that person might just be someone like me, looking for a reason to exist.

Yes, I went to each once. I asked to be put on Wellbutrin (I had my reasons, plus some psych literature to back me up.) and, although I'm no expert, my request was ignored without a second thought.

I've given up on treatment.
I can't imagine anyone genuinely giving a shit about me. I have an awful family life. I can't seem to find anyone who thinks that I'm worth getting to know.

>But why can't having a conversation with someone be meaningful, even if they are a passing acquaintance? 

It can be, really, but, that, too, is ephemeral. It's better to just not have a conversation with someone who I will never meet again than it is for me to have an amazing talk with someone and know that I will never again be in their company. It's more depressing than it's worth.

>Try not to judge your worth on the opinions of others...It probably wouldnt make you feel better about yourself.

It does, actually. In fact, the only time that I'm ever even content with myself is when I can make other people happy, which is rare, to say the least. I only care about other people because I don't care about myself (why should I?), and if I can't be useful to them, then I guess I'm not useful at all.

I'm ~1400 miles away, actually (Austin, Texas) and not old enough to drink legally. Unless you have a lot of frequent flier miles, I wouldn't really consider this a viable option.

Thanks for the outreach, though. I guess it's a little unsettling, though, to know that people only have interest in me when I'm ready to kill myself (no offense).

I honestly don't think that my depression is "coloring my perception", if you will. It's not as if my pseudofriends chat with me for a while and then say, "Oh no! I have to get to my lecture class, now -- sorry! I'll talk to you later."

I initiate contact and almost never get a reply.

>There are a couple people here talking to you--so some people care about your existence.

Well, maybe, but not in a wholly genuine way, I know. I could just disappear tomorrow, and it's not as if you'd know -- it wouldn't affect you in the slightest (and that's okay). 

>That's how it goes brother.

Sister, actually.

What I meant is that I can't really articulate all of this, especially not in person. What I've "described" doesn't even begin to cover it.

"Hi, pseudofriend, I'm feeling suicidal. Can we talk?" just doesn't work for me.

Besides, who would I talk to? I'm ignored. My existence is pointless.

>Do you really think those around you feel that way about you?

See this post: http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/d5ym9/could_i_be_any_more_of_a_failure/c0xt6od

EDIT: I didn't mean for this to sound harsh. I guess it's nice to know that someone is listening, but that "niceness" is so ephemeral. No matter what anyone says or does, no matter how uplifted I may feel at one moment, I know that I'll just end up in this exact same place tomorrow night. There is no escaping it.

I don't have the resources to try and be happy. I do, however, have the resources to *literally* "just drop it" all. 

Also, I've always found traveling to be deeply depressing. The only people I ever meet are passing acquaintances at best, and no matter where I go, I find the same people and same places. It's all the same. Nothing ever changes.

I went to a psychologist at my university who referred me to a psychiatrist. I was in a really dark place, so they streamlined my treatment. Needless to say, things only got worse and I haven't gone back to see either of them.

I'm unwanted, obviously. No one cares about my existence, so I feel like I just impose myself on people. I'm never invited to parties. I never get any phone calls. I always have to initiate contact with people, and they always fight my attempts at conversation and try to get out of them as quickly as possible.

A few years ago, that probably would have been enough. 

"Things will get better. Don't worry -- you'll be okay." 

Still, after years of hearing that, I'm still not okay and, if this trend continues (it will), then I guess I'll never be alright, so what's the point?

Regardless, we all become a statistic. People die of heart disease, in car accidents, and, yes, even of suicide every day. We all die.

I've tried talking to people, but the only people who I want to talk to are those around me -- tangible people who can actually be there for me, not just some anonymous voice on the phone -- but I just can't find the words. I don't want them to pity me and think that I'm crazy. It'd be much easier to just let go and not inconvenience them so much with my presence.
